key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINNs for Dirichlet boundary control of semilinear parabolic PDEs and, for the indirect method, proves a conditional error framework that links residuals and soft-constraint violations to solution error.
engineering_relevance: This gives a principled way to train neural PDE controllers while quantifying when PINN-based boundary control can be trusted for time-dependent diffusion-reaction systems.
method: Direct PINN: separate networks for state and control minimize a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: joint networks for state, adjoint, and control satisfy the first-order optimality system.
Error analysis: decomposes total error into approximation, optimization, quadrature, and soft boundary/terminal-constraint terms, with a computable residual indicator.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on two manufactured test problems—a cubic reaction-diffusion equation and a linear equation with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint—showing the behavior of both formulations.
watch_item: The error guarantees are conditional on regularity, approximation assumptions, soft-constraint control, and staying in a local neighborhood of the reference solution, so reliability may degrade outside that regime.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
